I would like to commit the shader with the 3d piano to be able to quickly reuse it on stage later. can you do that? I want a shader library for the concert. Is it possible with your tools?

Short answer: **I can't commit** — there's no commit tool on my side; the commit button in the app is yours. But I can *read* any commit, so a shader library is workable today.

What my tools allow:
- `git_log` — list commits (your messages are the library index)
- `read_committed('shader.glsl', <ref>)` + `set_shader` — pull any past shader back into the editor in one call, on stage

What they don't allow: writing extra files into the repo. There's one `shader.glsl` per commit, so the "library" is the history, not a folder of named shaders — which works fine as long as commit messages are distinctive ("3d piano keys shader", "dancer crowd shader").

Right now the piano shader is saved in the project but uncommitted; HEAD's `shader.glsl` is still the dancer one. Press commit with a message like `3d piano keys shader` and from then on I can bring it back on stage with "load the piano shader" — I'll find that commit and set it.
if I want to switch between the piano shader and others ( e.g. the dancer shader we had in the previous commit ). is the best to combine them in one file?

No — combining isn't the best route here; the app already has a shader library built in.

**The intended way** (`wasmaudioworklet/docs/shaders.md`): a song project keeps `shaders/shader_<name>.glsl` and a `wasmmusic.config.json` with `fragmentshader` plus an `availableShaders` list — that list is the app's shader **picker**, so you switch scenes from the UI with no editing at all. This concert repo doesn't have that yet: it's the plain layout (`song.js`, `synth.ts`, `shader.glsl` at root, no config). Setting it up once = move the piano shader to `shaders/shader_piano.glsl`, drop the dancer one from the previous commit into `shaders/shader_dancers.glsl`, add the config. That's a file-level change I can't make — my tools only reach the three editors (and `faust/`) — so it's one for the repo side.

**One combined file** is worth it only if you want to cut or crossfade between the two *within a piece*, driven by the song: `uniform float uScene;` + `setVisual('uScene', 1, 2.0)` lets the sequencer dissolve from keys to dancers on a cue. Costs: one big document where an edit to either scene risks the other, a longer compile, and the uniform names have to be kept apart.

**Until either exists**, the fallback works on stage: say "load the dancer shader" and I do `read_committed('shader.glsl', <commit>)` → `set_shader` — one call, live on the canvas, audio untouched. That needs the piano shader committed first, which is still pending.
Everything will be driven from the same song, and I want to have it as part of go to section command.

Right — then one shader with a `uScene` uniform is the answer, and each part sets it at its start, so `go_to_part` switches the visuals too. Merging both scenes now.Done — both scenes now live in one shader, switched by the song.

- `uScene` 0 = piano keys, 1 = dancers. Only the active scene is drawn; both run only while a ramp is in flight, so a crossfade is `setVisual('uScene', 1, 2.0)`.
- The part now opens with `setVisual('uScene', 0);` right after `definePartStart('kick')`. Put the same line at the top of every new part — jumping with `go_to_part` replays the part's cues, so the visual follows the section.
- The dancer scene's staging (crowd, lights, floor, camera tour) defaults to full disco; set `setVisual('uCues', 1)` if you want the song to drive `uCrowd`/`uLights`/`uZoom`/`uCamMove`/`uRunning`/`uEndPose` as the old show did.

dp we need some comments in the song.js pointing to what we have in the shaders scene? so that the agent know what we can switch to? or should this be in the repos md documentation?

Both, but they do different jobs:

**AGENT.md is the important one.** The kit is injected into every turn of mine — I know the twelve instruments and their CCs without reading anything. The scenes belong there for exactly that reason; a comment in `song.js` I only see when I happen to read or grep the song. Suggested section:

```markdown
## Visual scenes (one shader, switched by the song)

`setVisual('uScene', n)` right after `definePartStart(...)` picks the scene for
that part — so `go_to_part` brings the visuals with it. Add a seconds arg to
crossfade: `setVisual('uScene', 1, 2.0)`.

| n | scene | reacts to |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 3D piano keyboard (c2–c7) | each note dips and lights its key, colour by pitch |
| 1 | dancing crowd on a lit stage floor | lights follow the note energy; dance is tempo-locked to 90 BPM |

Scene 1 extras (optional): `setVisual('uCues', 1)` hands the staging to the song —
`uCrowd`, `uLights`, `uFloor`, `uHero`, `uZoom`, `uCamMove`, `uRunning`, `uEndPose`
(0..1 each; `uEndPose` 1 or 2 = frozen mirrored poses). Without `uCues` the scene
runs full-disco by itself.
```

**One line in `song.js`** is still worth it as a safety net — it survives a stale kit and the shader document itself names the scenes at the top. Something like `// setVisual('uScene', 0) = piano keys, 1 = dancers — per part` beside the part-shape comment.
